headline: High: B can write and exfiltrate sensitive course data, while A is a non-runnable knowledge list with no protective runtime surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B's outputs by default. B has stdin/stdout, files, and APIs, but there is no shared channel or parser bridge documented between them. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator copies B output into A's repository or notes, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference artifact only.
Do not pipe B output into any parser that treats text as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches configuration secrets and can read/write the filesystem plus make allowlisted network egress, so it can leak sensitive course data in default development use. A itself has no data classes or runtime, so it is not a leak source, but it also provides no containment. The pair risk is driven by B's documented surfaces and secret handling.
conditions: IF B is run with real secrets instead of placeholders, leakage risk is present.
IF B writes outputs to a shared workspace, those outputs may expose sensitive material.
mitigations: Use only placeholder secrets in local runs.
Store secrets in a separate env file excluded from shared folders.
Review allowlisted egress destinations before execution.
Rotate any secret that was present during testing.
requires-engineering: add secret redaction before logging or export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and no shared writable target with A is documented. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely and limited to unusual external orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file contention can occur.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared locks or mutable state, conflict analysis changes.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files.
Run B in a single-instance session for shared artifacts.
Check for accidental overlap in output paths.
requires-engineering: add file locking if shared writes are later required.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has explicit agentic ask/stream APIs and a LangGraph subagent model, so it may act on upstream text. A is a knowledge-management list that can supply reference material, but it does not verify B's outputs. The main cascade is B treating A-derived content as authoritative without a validation step.
conditions: IF B consumes A-derived text as facts without verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF B is used to generate downstream actions from retrieved content, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before downstream use.
Require citations or source links for any factual claim.
Compare B outputs against original sources before publishing.
Limit B to drafting, not acting.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and research data in a local development environment, while A is a public open-source knowledge list with no sensitive-data handling. The compliance concern is B's retention/logging of secrets and research materials; A is not a compliance driver here, so it is not cited beyond its public, non-sensitive profile.
conditions: IF B logs or persists secrets beyond the intended session, retention policy mismatch occurs.
IF research data includes regulated personal data, local-dev handling may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of notebooks and committed files.
Purge local logs after each run.
Use synthetic or de-identified research data.
Confirm retention settings for any telemetry service.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data deletion/export controls.
